accepted.label: Strategic Discipline for AI-Augmented Decision-Making
accepted.description: Before integrating AI into decisions, organizations should treat decision-making as a strategic discipline and intentionally design human-machine relationships.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain why decision-making must be treated as a strategic discipline when adopting AI.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as a distinct teachable concept about the prerequisite of strategic discipline.

accepted.label: Preserving Human Agency in AI Decisions
accepted.description: Maintain human agency by building accountability, ensuring decision-makers understand (not just comply with) AI outputs, and clearly connecting choices to choosers.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe at least two concrete ways to preserve human agency when AI supports decisions.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as a distinct set of design principles for human agency.

accepted.label: Human Purpose and Judgment as Irreplaceable by AI
accepted.description: Technology can speed up analysis and reduce uncertainty, but it cannot substitute human purpose, values, and judgment behind choices.
coverage_criteria: Student can articulate at least one reason why human purpose and judgment remain essential even when AI provides analysis.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as a philosophical limit of AI in decision-making.

accepted.label: Building Decision-Making Competence for Humans and AI
accepted.description: Organizations should simultaneously invest in developing human decision-making skills and rigorously measuring AI decision performance.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe one approach to improve human decision skill and one approach to measure AI decision performance.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as a dual focus on human and machine competence.

accepted.label: Risk-Based AI Agency Level
accepted.description: The degree of autonomy granted to AI agents should be calibrated according to the risk profile of the decision.
coverage_criteria: Student can justify why a high-risk decision warrants lower AI autonomy.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate stands alone as a specific design principle for AI autonomy levels.
